text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert INC-20123 — service=ingress-proxy severity=P1. Elevated 5xx rate + timeout spike. Page routed to on-call: Alice. Link: https://pager.company/INC-20123 :rotating_light:

Alice: Acked. I'm on it. Starting triage — will gather quick metrics and correlation ids.

Ben: Thanks — I'm available to take over if this escalates. Quick Q: is this global or region-specific?

Alice: Initial metrics from the dashboard show spikes in us-west-2 and us-east-1. Latency climbs ~300ms, error rate from ~0.2% -> 6%.

Carla: I'm seeing a pattern of 502s in the ingress proxy logs with this header: `X-Correlation-Id`. Sending a small sample.

Carla: ```
[2026-03-15T05:12:21.123Z] INFO request_id=3f6a2c X-Correlation-Id=cf2b-9a1 ingress=ingress-proxy upstream=upstream-a status=502 duration=12ms "GET /v1/gen"
[2026-03-15T05:12:22.045Z] INFO request_id=3f6a2d X-Correlation-Id=cf2b-9a2 ingress=ingress-proxy upstream=upstream-b status=502 duration=8ms "POST /v1/chat"
[2026-03-15T05:12:23.511Z] WARN request_id=3f6a2e X-Correlation-Id=cf2b-9a3 ingress=ingress-proxy upstream=upstream-a status=504 duration=1500ms "POST /v1/embeddings"
```

Dan: Correlation IDs line up with a rollback we did around 05:10 for upstream-a. Could be related. I can pull the deploy timeline.

Alice: Good catch. Dan: can you paste the deploy id and git hash? Also capture upstream service health.

Dan: Deploy: svc-upstream-a @ rev 1a2b3c4d — rolled at 05:09:58 UTC (canary -> 100%). Rollback trigger not executed automatically.

Emily: I see pods for upstream-a restarting around 05:11. Kube events show OOMKilled on 2 replicas. Logs show repeated `unhandledException` in the request handler.

Carla: Adding to timeline: 05:09:58 deploy upstream-a -> 05:11 restarts -> 05:12 ingress 5xx spike starts. Hypothesis: new upstream release has a bug causing crashes under a specific request pattern.

Ben: Hypothesis list (tracking):
- H1: upstream-a release regression causing crashes/OOMs (active)
- H2: ingress proxy misconfiguration causing header parsing errors (low)
- H3: networking flake between proxy and upstream (medium)

Alice: Running quick query for requests with `X-Correlation-Id` prefix `cf2b-` across all proxies to estimate customer impact.

Alice: Query result: 14,924 requests with that prefix in the 5m window; 1,020 failed (6.8%). Affected customer segments: hosted API / free tier (bulk) and 3 dedicated tenants showing higher-than-usual error rate.

SRE-Oncall: Customer impact table — 3 dedicated customers with >15% error rate for that window. Recommend immediate mitigation: route traffic for affected tenants to fallback pool (upstream-b) and rollback upstream-a to previous stable revision if confirmed.

Dan: I can roll back upstream-a now to rev 0f9e8d7c. Approving: Alice?

Alice: Please proceed with rollback. Also open a maintenance window and notify the console about degraded availability for the affected tenants.

Dan: Executing rollback command:```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/upstream-a --to-revision=2
# waiting for pods to come up
```

Carla: While rollback is in progress, I'm adding a temporary routing rule to divert traffic that contains `X-Tenant: dedicated-` to upstream-b. Patch:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  route_rule: "if X-Tenant startswith dedication- then backend upstream-b"
```

Ben: Heads-up: modifying routing rules will cause a short reconvergence but should be fine. I've pre-approved the change.

Alice: Rollback completed at ~05:19:30 UTC, pods are stable. Early metrics: error rate dropped from 6.8% -> 0.4% in the last 2 minutes. Great.

Emily: Confirmed — OOMKilled events stop after rollback. Upstream-a logs on bad revision show a memory leak increasing RSS on specific request patterns.

Carla: Marking H1 as confirmed (regression). H2/H3 deprioritized.

SRE-Oncall: Noting mitigation: rollback + routing diversion. Action items:
- Action A: postmortem write-up (owner: Alice)
- Action B: add admission gate for upstream releases that run heap smoke test (owner: Emily)
- Action C: add correlation-id sampling to retention pipeline for better triage (owner: Ben)

Ben: For the RCA thread: please paste any full correlation IDs you captured. I'll stitch logs across services. Example we used above: `cf2b-9a1`, `cf2b-9a2`, `cf2b-9a3`. If anyone has a full request_id that ties to the handler exception, paste it here.

Emily: Full request_id sample: `3f6a2e-7b9c-20260315`. Stack trace snippet from upstream-a (bad revision):```
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
  at com.redwood.inference.handlers.RequestProcessor.process(RequestProcessor.java:412)
  at com.redwood.inference.server.HttpAdapter.handle(HttpAdapter.java:88)
```

Alice: Customer comms: I'm drafting a status update: short note that we saw elevated 5xx due to a bad upstream release; rollback completed and services stabilized; dedicated tenants experienced intermittent errors. I'll post to status page and message affected customers via the account team.

Carla: Adding post-incident logs to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-20123/ — includes ingress logs, upstream-a logs (bad rev), kube events, and the correlation id list.

Dan: Handing off on-call to Ben at 05:30 UTC for postmortem and follow-ups. Ben: you have the lead.

Ben: Got it — taking over. I'll own the RCA, run a bisect to identify problematic commit, and coordinate fixes. Will schedule a follow-up 1hr post-incident sync.

Alice: Thank you all. Final note — monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to reduce noise but keep signal for release-induced spikes.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20123 acknowledged by Ben. Recorded timeline, mitigations, and initial owner assignments. Please file the postmortem using the incident template and link here. :white_check_mark:
